description: Climate and Hazard Mitigation Planning (CHaMP) Tool is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NOAA Climate Program Office; Urban Sustainability Directors Network; Carolinas Integrated Sciences and Assessments. This tool supports the development of climate-informed Infrastructure and Hazard Mitigation Plans required by FEMA. The tool provides users with community- and region-specific historical and projected climate and hazard information for the following themes: Coastal Hazards, Extreme Rainfall/Flooding, Fog, Great Lakes Hazards, Severe Weather, Tropical Storms/Hurricanes, Extreme Heat, Wildfire, and Winter Weather. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Changing Seasons, Extreme Heat, Flooding – Coastal, Flooding – General, Severe Winter Weather, Wildfire. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Economy, Energy and Utilities, People, Property. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
